legend: After studying the "Matrix Bel Lotus", Muhannad (not you, Nahhal) invented a new concept in numbers, the lotusency. The lotusency of an integer Y$$$Y$$$ is the number of times it can be square-rooted while still remaining an integer. For example:
Lotusency of 5$$$5$$$ is 0$$$0$$$ because its square-root is not an integer.
Muhannad has an integer X$$$X$$$, and he wants to maximize its lotusency. He can do the following operation at most K$$$K$$$ times:
Choose any prime number p$$$p$$$ and set X=X⋅p$$$X = X \cdot p$$$.
What is the maximum lotusency he can obtain?
input: The first line contains a single integer tc(1≤tc≤2⋅105)$$$tc \: (1 \leq tc \leq 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the number of testcases.
The first and only line of each testcase consists of two integers X,K(2≤X≤2⋅105)(0≤K≤1018)$$$X,K \: (2 \leq X \leq 2 \cdot 10^5) (0 \leq K \leq 10^{18})$$$.
output: For each testcase, print a single integer, the maximum lotusency Muhannad can obtain.
